title: Pulse restored, now what?
note: Fictional patient. Doses and energies are quoted from the 2025 AHA guidelines (and the ERC where named) for recognition; your unit protocol, crash-cart stock and the attending nephrologist come first. Simulation success is an educational result, not a prediction of patient survival.
intro: After 11 minutes of CPR, Mr. Leonardo Ramos, 70, has a carotid pulse at a freestanding unit in Taytay. Pressure 84/50, saturation 89% on a mask, irregular breathing, not following commands. The ambulance is 20 minutes away. A nurse asks, “Should we put him back on dialysis while we wait?”

choices.text: Keep pads on; support breathing with the bag-mask and oxygen to 90 to 98%; saline per physician toward a MAP of at least 65; 12-lead ECG; glucose and potassium.
choices.feedback: AHA 2025 post-ROSC targets for oxygen and pressure, plus dialysis-specific checks.

choices.text: Remove the pads to make him comfortable.
No, not without the attending nephrologist; he is unstable and needs monitored care. Call the attending and the receiving hospital.
choices.feedback: Card 1: do not restart dialysis unless the attending says so.

choices.text: Yes, reconnect to finish the session.
choices.feedback: Starting a circuit in an unstable patient can drop the pressure and cause re-arrest.

choices.text: Re-arrest: compressions within seconds, arrest algorithm from the recorder’s last rhythm and drug times.
choices.feedback: Pads on and a running timeline make re-arrest fast to treat.

choices.text: Check the blood pressure cuff again.

n4.scene: After one shock, ROSC again; pressure 98/60. The ambulance arrives.

choices.text: Identity, time of collapse, rhythms, shocks, drugs and times, ROSC times; hours on machine, 2.6 L removed, blood returned, last potassium; current vitals; ECG and sheets.
choices.feedback: The arrest and dialysis facts travel together.

choices.text: “He arrested and we got him back.”
choices.feedback: Without the dialysis facts and times, the receiving team starts over.
choices.then: The recorder hands over the full sheet.

end.title: 3:05 p.m.
end.text: Mr. Ramos leaves with a full handover. The debrief adds a one-page post-ROSC handover sheet to the crash cart.

debrief:
What this case teaches

  • After ROSC: oxygen 90 to 98%, MAP at least 65, ECG, glucose, potassium, pads on.
  • No dialysis restart without the attending nephrologist.
  • Hand over the arrest and the dialysis facts together.
